bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Caribbean Conservation Association (CCA) "exists to enhance the quality of life for present and future generations of the Caribbean by facilitating the development and implementation of policies, programmes and practices, which contribute to the sustainable management of the region's natural and cultural resources

The CCA began in Barbados in the late 1960s in part with funding and support from Laurance Rockefeller to create the Caribbean's first regional institution focused on the environment. The CCA also received funding from the Rockefeller Brothers Fund (RBF), particularly during the 1970s and 80s as well as the American Conservation Association (ACA).
The CCA closed operations in 2003 and at that time the records were given to a sister organization in the country, the Barbados National Trust.

scopecontent.p: The collection is comprised of administrative and operation records, as well as a selection of publications.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Publications were another significant part of this collection. There were two main types of publications. The first of these were publications by the Caribbean Conservation Association (CCA) itself (sometimes on its own and sometimes in cooperation with other organizations such as the Island Resources Foundation (IRF)). These publications came in the form of both reports and other scientific publications and others that were made for public consumption such as newsletters, brochures, and teacher's guides. The other type of publication was those done by other organizations. Most of these had been part of the CCA's extensive library, which was one of their main programs. The association was known for their library which collected works related to environmental concerns and programs related to the Caribbean as a whole. They would then provide copies of any of the sources to those who asked. Some of those requests for information were found in the CCA records. In addition to books, reports and articles, they also included pamphlets/brochures, clippings and vertical files, etc. Some of these publications related to smaller and more regional organizations whose work may not be documented elsewhere.
